Sumimi v0.4.0 — the admission gate, and six platforms.

**The gate.** The collection API has a front door now. Four limits, all
adjustable, with the defaults derived from the memory budget:

| limit | default | environment variable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| request rate | 20 000/s per 128 MB of the engine's budget (40 000/s at 256 MB) | `SUMIMI_MAX_ADMIT_RPS` |
| body size | 2 MB | `SUMIMI_MAX_BODY_BYTES` |
| requests in flight | off | `SUMIMI_MAX_INFLIGHT_REQUESTS` |
| bytes in flight | off | `SUMIMI_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES` |

A request over the rate is refused with **503** and a `Retry-After` header; a
body over the size limit is refused with **413**. The heartbeat
(`/api/heartbeat`) reports what the gate did: the requests and the bytes in
flight, and the refusals by reason (`refusedRate`, `refusedInflight`,
`refusedBody`).

**Why.** The write path is the memory. Measured on two machines, the peak
resident set grows by about 8 MB for every 1 000 requests a second of offered
traffic — and the machine only decides how far up that rate axis you can go.
A server that is asked for more than it can write grows until the kernel kills
it. The gate turns that into a refusal the client can retry, and the default
is set from the engine's memory budget: a 512 MB box gets the 128 MB tier
(20 000/s), a 1 GB box gets 256 MB (40 000/s). The rule and the measurements
are in the new **Memory** page of the documentation.

**Six archives.** macOS, Linux and Windows, each in arm64 and x64 — every one
of them built on a runner of its own architecture, so DuckDB is compiled
natively for the target:

| platform | file |
| --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Darwin-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Intel) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Darwin-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (x86-64) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (ARM64) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Linux-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| Windows (x86-64) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Windows-x86_64.zip` |
| Windows (ARM64) | `sumimi-v0.4.0-Windows-aarch64.zip` |

Each archive holds the `sumimi` binary (the server and the client in one
file), the dashboard frontend, the documentation and the licence.

Unpack it and run it:

```bash
sumimi serve --dir ./sumimi --port 3000
```
